module

public import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Erdős Problem 424: Sequence generated by $a_i a_j - 1$

*References:*
 - [erdosproblems.com/424](https://www.erdosproblems.com/424)
 - [A5244](https://oeis.org/A5244)
 - [Ben Green's Open Problem 63](https://people.maths.ox.ac.uk/greenbj/papers/open-problems.pdf#section.8 Problem 63)
 - [Ko26] Korsky, S., *A problem of Erdős on the sequence $a_ia_j - 1$*,
   [arXiv:2608.07910](https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.07910)
-/

@[expose] public section

namespace Erdos424

open Set

/--
Defines the set of new numbers generated from a set A by the operation
$x y - 1$ for $x \neq y$.
-/
def nextGeneration (A : Set ℕ) : Set ℕ :=
  { z : ℕ | ∃ x y, x ∈ A ∧ y ∈ A ∧ x ≠ y ∧ z = x * y - 1 }

/--
The sequence of sets $A_n$ where $A_0 = \{2, 3\}$ and $A_{n+1}$ is $A_n$ union all newly
generated elements.
-/
def sequenceSet : ℕ → Set ℕ
  | 0 => {2, 3}
  | n + 1 => (sequenceSet n) ∪ (nextGeneration (sequenceSet n))

/-- The set of integers which eventually appear in the sequence, which is the union of all $A_n$. -/
def generatedSet : Set ℕ := ⋃ n : ℕ, sequenceSet n

/--
Let $a_1 = 2$ and $a_2 = 3$ and continue the sequence by appending to $a_1, \ldots, a_n$ all possible
values of $a_i a_j - 1$ with $i \neq j$.
Is it true that the set of integers which eventually appear has positive density?

As explained on [erdosproblems.com/424](https://www.erdosproblems.com/424), "positive density"
here means positive *lower* density: is there $c > 0$ such that for all large $x$ at least
$cx$ of the integers in $[1, x]$ appear? See `erdos_424.variants.exact_density` for the
literal reading.

Korsky [Ko26] has announced a proof that the set has positive lower density; it is listed
as a proof claim on [erdosproblems.com/424](https://www.erdosproblems.com/424), which still
records the problem as open.
-/
@[category research open, AMS 11]
theorem erdos_424 : answer(sorry) ↔ 0 < generatedSet.lowerDensity := by
  sorry

/--
A literal interpretation of "positive density": the natural density of `generatedSet` exists
(i.e. the lower and upper density agree) and is positive.
-/
@[category research open, AMS 11]
theorem erdos_424.variants.exact_density : answer(sorry) ↔ generatedSet.HasPosDensity := by
  sorry

-- TODO(firsching): formalize the statements from the additional material

end Erdos424

findings.description: The [Ko26] reference in the module docstring gives arXiv:2608.07910 the title “A problem of Erdős on the sequence a_i a_j − 1”. The cited paper is titled “Positive Lower Density for Hofstadter's ab−1 Problem”. The author, identifier, and mathematical attribution are correct; this is only a bibliographic slip.
findings.source_evidence: https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.07910 and the downloaded TeX source both give the title “Positive Lower Density for Hofstadter's $ab-1$ Problem”, by Samuel Korsky. OEIS A005244 lists the same title.
findings.suggested_fix: Replace the italicized title in the [Ko26] bibliography entry with the cited paper's actual title. No mathematical declaration needs changing.

reformulations.difference: Lean constructs a union of finite-stage sets in ℕ, whereas Korsky describes the smallest set of positive integers containing 2 and 3 and closed under ab−1 for distinct elements.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: The stages are nested, so any two elements of the union occur together at the maximum of their stages; their allowed product-minus-one occurs at the next stage. Conversely, induction shows every stage lies in any closed set containing the seeds. Every generated element is at least 2, so using ℕ introduces neither zero nor one, and natural-number subtraction agrees with integer subtraction on all generated inputs. The least-closure characterization and equivalence with finite derivations were proved in the scratch file.

reformulations.difference: Lean uses positivity of the liminf of # (generatedSet ∩ [0,n)) / n. The source expresses this as existence of c > 0 such that # (generatedSet ∩ [1,x]) ≥ cx for every sufficiently large real x.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: The partial densities lie in [0,1], and zero is not generated. Positive liminf is equivalent to an eventual positive uniform lower bound. Shifting the integer endpoint and passing between integer and real cutoffs via the floor function preserve existence of such a bound, with the constant reduced if necessary. The full equivalence with the real-cutoff counting statement was proved as Review424.generated_lower_pos_iff_source in /workspace/review/scratch.lean.

review.notes: All three definitions and both question statements were checked. No mathematical misformalization was found. The exact_density variant correctly asks the explicitly stronger question of existence of a positive natural density; it is not asserted equivalent to positive lower density. Small generated sets were checked in Lean, and bounded generation matched all 55 OEIS terms through 249. The Erdős page still records OPEN and explicitly treats Korsky's submission as a proof claim, consistent with the file's status and docstring. The scratch equivalence proofs do not depend on the conjectures' sorry proofs.
